**SpaceX Crew-11** was the eleventh operational NASA [Commercial Crew Program](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercial_Crew_Program "Commercial Crew Program") flight and the 19th crewed orbital flight of a [Crew Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crew_Dragon "Crew Dragon") spacecraft. The mission transported four crew members, [NASA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NASA "NASA") astronauts [Zena Cardman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zena_Cardman "Zena Cardman") and [Michael Fincke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Fincke "Michael Fincke"), [JAXA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JAXA "JAXA") astronaut [Kimiya Yui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimiya_Yui "Kimiya Yui"), and [Roscosmos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roscosmos "Roscosmos") cosmonaut [Oleg Platonov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Platonov_(cosmonaut) "Oleg Platonov (cosmonaut)"), to the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") (ISS). The mission launched on August 1, 2025 and docked with the ISS the next day. On January 8, 2026, NASA announced that the mission would end about a month earlier than planned due to a medical situation involving Fincke.

excerpts.text:
Four crew members of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11 mission launched at 11:43 a.m. EDT Friday from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida for a science expedition aboard the International Space Station.

A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket propelled the Dragon spacecraft into orbit carrying NASA astronauts Zena Cardman and Mike Fincke, JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) astronaut Kimiya Yui, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Oleg Platonov.

The number of crew aboard the space station will increase to 11 for a short time as Crew-11 joins NASA astronauts Anne McClain, Nichole Ayers, and Jonny Kim, JAXA astronaut Takuya Onishi, and Roscosmos cosmonauts Kirill Peskov, Sergey Ryzhikov, and Alexey Zubritsky.

excerpts.text: On March 27, 2025, Cardman was announced as the commander of the [SpaceX Crew-11](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Crew-11 "SpaceX Crew-11") mission that launched on August 1, 2025.

This event necessitated the early return of Crew-11, the first "controlled medical evacuation" of the International Space Station.[[13]](#cite_note-13) Alongside crewmates [Kimiya Yui](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimiya_Yui "Kimiya Yui") and [Christopher Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Williams_(astronaut) "Christopher Williams (astronaut)"), Cardman received NASA's Exceptional Bravery Medal[[14]](#cite_note-14) for "exceptional courage, leadership, and composure that directly contributed to the preservation of a crewmember's life".[[15]](#cite_note-15) After 167 days in space, Cardman brought Crew-11 and their Dragon spacecraft home. They safely splashed down on January 15, 2026.[[16]](#cite_note-:2-16)

excerpts.text: ![Expedition 73 welcomes NASA's SpaceX Crew-11 mission aboard the International Space Station. In the front from left are, Crew-11 members Oleg Platonov, Mike Fincke, Zena Cardman, and Kimiya Yui. In the back are, Expedition 73 members Takuya Onishi, Kirill Peskov, Alexey Zubritsky, Sergey Ryzhikov, Jonny Kim, Nichole Ayers, and Anne McClain.](https://www.nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/blog-exp73-11-member-crew-080425.jpg?w=2048)

[Expedition 73](https://www.nasa.gov/mission/expedition-73/) expanded to eleven individuals on Saturday when [NASA’s SpaceX Crew-11](https://www.nasa.gov/mission/nasas-spacex-crew-11/) mission [docked](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/2025/08/02/crew-11-docks-to-station-aboard-spacex-dragon/) to the orbital outpost aboard the Dragon spacecraft after [launching](https://www.nasa.gov/blogs/spacestation/2025/08/01/nasas-spacex-crew-11-launches-to-international-space-station/) from Florida about 15 hours earlier. Crew 11’s Commander and Pilot, [Zena Cardman](https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/astronauts/zena-cardman/) and [Mike Fincke](https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/astronauts/michael-e-fincke/), both from NASA, and Mission Specialists Kimiya Yui from JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) and Oleg Platonov from Roscosmos spent the weekend unpacking their Dragon spacecraft, reviewing safety procedures, and getting familiar with space station systems.

NASA astronauts [Anne McClain](https://www.nasa.gov/people/anne-c-mcclain/) and [Nichole Ayers](https://www.nasa.gov/people/nasa-astronaut-nichole-ayers/) along with JAXA astronaut Takuya Onishi and Roscosmos cosmonaut Kirill Peskov are helping their new crewmates get up to speed with living and working on the orbital lab. [NASA’s SpaceX Crew-10](https://www.nasa.gov/mission/crew-10/) crewmates also will be going home this week aboard another Dragon spacecraft completing a five-month mission.
